note: Trigger does not reach the defect, but not for the reason first recorded. The 2026-10-11 note said sqlite3Fts3Offsets runs twice and all three fts3EvalRestart calls come after both of them. Probe site 45, which marks the save (fts3ExprTermOffsetInit), the invalidate (fts3EvalRestart) and the read in one run, shows otherwise: SAVE x2, 6 reads, SAVE, RESTART, SAVE, 4 reads -- one restart, inside the second call rather than after both. What makes the trigger harmless is that every group of reads is preceded by its own save: the restart is followed by a fresh fts3ExprTermOffsetInit, so the four reads after it use pointers taken after it, never the ones it invalidated. Identical line for line on native memsys5 and on virtual Capstone with lookaside off. The distinction matters for anyone writing a trigger that does reach it: moving a restart earlier is not enough, it has to fall between a save and a read. Upstream 51dd67080a does the opposite, cancelling the incremental phrases before the pointers are taken (sqlite3Fts3MsrCancel from a new fts3ExprRestartIfCb). Measured 2026-10-16; host ASan is silent and all three arms report MISSED, none of which is a miss.
